Dans les anciens accords, l'écart qui re: In the old tunings, the leftover gap fell on a single fifth. Its beats made it howl like a wolf, hence its name. So one keyboard could not serve every key, and Baroque musicians sometimes retuned in the middle of a concert.

La « main guidonienne », qui place les n: The “Guidonian hand,” which places the notes on the joints of the fingers, bears the name of Guido of Arezzo. Yet it only spread after his death, and two authors who commented on Guido shortly after him do not even mention his syllables.

En mai 1939, à la Broadcasting House de: In May 1939, at Broadcasting House in London, European delegates agreed on an A at 440 Hz. Before that, everyone had their own: France had set itself 435 Hz in the 19th century. ISO adopted 440 in 1955, then made it the ISO 16 standard in 1975.

En 1547, à Bâle, Heinrich Glaréan porte: In 1547, in Basel, Heinrich Glarean took the church modes from eight to twelve in his Dodecachordon, adding the Ionian and Aeolian, our major and minor. Eleven years later, Zarlino took up his system in the Istitutioni harmoniche, without naming Glarean.

Joseph Sauveur a donné leur nom aux sons: Joseph Sauveur gave their names to harmonic sounds and to the nodes of strings in a 1701 paper. He also proposed a new science, devoted to sounds in general, and named it acoustics. His words are still in use.

Après Hippolyte et Aricie, en 1733, Pari: After Hippolyte et Aricie, in 1733, Paris split. Lully's supporters found Rameau's harmonies discordant and saw them as an attack on French music; Rameau's supporters, the “Rameauneurs,” defended him. The pamphlet war lasted until the end of the decade.

La flûte de Hohle Fels a été taillée dan: The Hohle Fels flute was carved from a vulture's radius. Found in 2006, it is among the oldest known instruments: five holes drilled about 35,000 years ago, long before farming and writing.

L'hymne à Nikkal est la plus vieille mus: The hymn to Nikkal is the oldest substantially complete notated music, around 1400 BC. But its interval names and numbers have received at least five rival decipherments: depending on the scholar, the same tablet sings five different tunes.

La tombe du marquis Yi de Zeng a été tro: The tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng was found in 1977 by soldiers levelling a hill to build a factory. Inside, 65 bronze bells that each give two notes, buried for twenty-four centuries.

Boèce a écrit sa Consolation de Philosop: Boethius wrote his Consolation of Philosophy in prison, awaiting execution in 524. His music treatise was copied in about 140 manuscripts and taught throughout the Middle Ages.

Pérotin a écrit vers 1198 de la musique: Pérotin wrote four-voice music for Notre-Dame in Paris around 1198. We know his name only thanks to an English student who took notes around 1275, and whose own name is unknown: historians call him Anonymous IV.

En 1498, Petrucci demande au doge de Ven: In 1498, Petrucci asked the doge of Venice for twenty years' monopoly on music printing. It took him three years to bring out his first book, the Odhecaton, dated 15 May 1501.

Dietrich Nikolaus Winkel invente à Amste: Dietrich Nikolaus Winkel invented a spring pendulum to beat time in Amsterdam in 1814. Johann Maelzel added a scale, patented it in 1815 and sold it under his name: scores still say M.M., Maelzel's Metronome.

Schoenberg had a phobia of the number 13. Born on 13 September, he dreaded dying in a year that was a multiple of 13. He died on Friday 13 July 1951, shortly before midnight.

Le thérémine est né en 1920 de recherche: The theremin was born in 1920 from Soviet research on proximity sensors. Its two antennas pick up no radio: they are position sensors, and the note is the difference between two oscillators.
